second_order: making Bill and other Gravity Falls marks
theme_note: These codes hold together because people place, propose, locate, or take credit for visible Gravity Falls marks. What varies is the mark—Bill, a pine tree, zodiac, joaje, or the subreddit name—and whether the turn starts, joins, or reports the work.

These codes hold together because participants keep an existing Bill intact against erasure, alteration, or the Void. They vary from one-pixel upkeep and eye repair to warnings, restraint, and urgent defence calls.

second_order: doing the room's April Fools joking
theme_note: These codes hold together because subreddit participants tease, dupe, warn, or play along with April Fools inside the room. The jokes range from a fake Season 3 announcement to general suspicion; none is about the canvas.

These codes hold together because people turn an idea into a workable design by asking how, scaling it down or up, and choosing what version or missing feature to use. What varies is whether feasibility, ambition, or appearance is at issue.

second_order: negotiating space and keeping the peace
theme_note: These codes hold together because people explain borders, request truces, respect neighbours, halt expansion, accept corrections, and offer reciprocal help. What varies is the neighbour and whether the exchange prevents overlap, repairs a misunderstanding, or establishes coexistence.

These codes hold together because participants direct coordination away from the subreddit into Discord or use Discord to rally builders. They vary between an early invitation for the original canvas and later coordination after the build moved to clones.
This single code calls the room to retaliate against r/NuclearThrone's challenge; it belongs with no other practice because later replies reject rather than extend that call.

second_order: mourning Bill and promising to rebuild
theme_note: These codes hold together because people name Bill's loss, say RIP, ask whether he recovered, or promise that he will return. What varies is whether the loss is unfolding, recalled after the canvas closes, or turned immediately into a rebuild pledge.

These codes hold together because participants continue the project after r/place by starting, joining, crediting, or publicising Bill on PlaceTwo and pxls.space. What varies is the clone, the degree of completion, and whether the turn recruits help or reports work done.
This single surviving title congratulates the room on its Bill, while the deleted image leaves whether the canvas is meant uncertain.
